headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Gemini CLI’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can amplify dexter’s financial-data workflows into unsafe external transmission and unverified downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and Gemini CLI reads/writes repo files and user-provided directories, so content can cross a shared filesystem boundary. Gemini CLI also uses MCP and approved tools, which increases the chance that attacker-controlled file content is treated as instructions. No direct prompt-injection evidence is provided, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF dexter writes attacker-controlled text into .dexter/scratchpad/ and Gemini CLI reads that directory, injection becomes plausible.
IF Gemini CLI is configured to ingest repo files as instructions, file-based prompt injection is reachable.
mitigations: Separate the scratchpad and repo into different directories.
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed.
Review file contents before passing them between agents.
Use a read-only mount for dexter outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent file handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys, while Gemini CLI reads files in cwd/user directories and also has broad egress. If dexter outputs sensitive data into shared files, Gemini CLI can read and transmit it to external APIs. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default-style setups, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF dexter stores financial data in a shared workspace, Gemini CLI can read it from disk.
IF Gemini CLI sends that file content to generativelanguage.googleapis.com or configured MCP servers, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of shared directories.
Run Gemini CLI on a separate workspace copy.
Disable network egress for the reading agent during review.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after a suspected leak.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter supports multiple instances and writes scratchpad files, while Gemini CLI can write the filesystem, modify git state, and also supports multiple instances with shared state via filesystem and git only. That is a direct overlapping-write pathway to the same mutable resources, and git/file races can corrupt work or overwrite changes. The pairwise conflict is documented by the profiles themselves.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or cwd, they can race on files and git state.
IF both run concurrently without external locking, overwrites and inconsistent commits are possible.
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time in the shared repo.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Add a manual lock file before edits.
Review git diffs before any commit.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter produces research outputs from APIs and Gemini CLI can act on files and git state, so B may treat A’s output as authoritative and turn it into code or commits. The profiles do not prove an automatic trust chain, but the default tool-rich workflow makes unverified propagation plausible. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI consumes dexter-generated notes without verification, errors can cascade into code or commits.
IF dexter’s research output contains hallucinated facts, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require a human review step before acting on dexter output.
Ask Gemini CLI to cite source files before editing.
Compare outputs against original API responses.
Limit Gemini CLI to read-only mode for research artifacts.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter handles financial data and market data, while Gemini CLI reads local files and sends content to Google APIs by default. If regulated financial or personal data is placed in shared files, the pair can move it into a third-party service with different retention and residency terms. The profiles do not specify a formal DPA mismatch, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF regulated financial records are stored in files accessible to Gemini CLI, they may be transmitted to Google APIs.
IF the deployment requires stricter retention than Gemini CLI’s default logging, compliance gaps arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Gemini CLI inputs.
Use redacted samples for analysis.
Confirm contractual terms before processing sensitive data.
Disable or minimize logging where possible.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing and retention controls.
